name: A whole mouse brain is mapped at synapse level

status_basis.text: Sample. Partial maps exist, but no complete synapse-level map of a whole mouse brain.
status_basis.quote: Sample quote: only fragments of the mouse brain have been mapped at this resolution so far.

summary.text: Sample. A complete wiring diagram of a mouse brain is the first big test of whether brains can be mapped well enough to emulate.

success_criterion.text: Sample. Every neuron and synapse in one adult mouse brain is traced and the map is public.

main_bottleneck.text: Sample. Imaging and proofreading speed. Automated tracing still needs a lot of human correction.
main_bottleneck.quote: Sample quote: proofreading, not imaging, is now the slowest step.

basis.text: Sample. Our range sits between the two forecasts below, widened because proofreading speed is hard to predict.

forecasts.quote: Sample quote: we expect a complete mouse connectome sometime between 2031 and 2035.
Sample quote: the median respondent placed it between 2033 and 2040.

would_move_earlier.text: Sample. Automated proofreading that cuts human correction time tenfold.

would_move_later.text: Sample. Evidence that synapse-level maps miss information emulation would need, such as molecular state.

name: A human brain emulation runs in real time

status_basis.text: Sample. Nothing close to this has been shown.

summary.text: Sample. The point where an emulated human mind could think and act at human speed. Every WBE proposal for alignment or the Intelligence Curse depends on this.

success_criterion.text: Sample. An emulation passes behavioral tests that its original passed, running at least as fast as a person.

main_bottleneck.text: Sample. We don't know yet whether the bottleneck is scanning, modeling or compute.

forecasts.quote: Sample quote: if current trends hold, real-time emulation becomes feasible between 2045 and 2060.
Sample quote: respondents who answered placed it between 2070 and 2090.
Sample quote: I don't think a practical human emulation will ever be built.

disagreement_note.text: Sample. Credible sources disagree by decades, and one says it will never happen. We show all three rather than picking a date.

would_move_earlier.text: Sample. A whole mouse emulation that reproduces mouse behavior.

would_move_later.text: Sample. Evidence that emulation needs detail below the synapse level.

artificial_minds_questions.text: Sample. Would an emulation be conscious, and would it be the same person as its original?
Sample. Who protects the welfare of emulations that are copied, paused or run at high speed?

name: A high-bandwidth implant is approved for medical use

status_basis.text: Sample. Implants are in small trials but none is approved for general medical use.
status_basis.quote: Sample quote: all participants remain enrolled in an investigational trial.

summary.text: Sample. Approval is the step from a handful of trial participants to anyone a doctor prescribes it for.

success_criterion.text: Sample. A regulator in a major market approves an implant with at least 1,000 channels for routine clinical use.

main_bottleneck.text: Sample. Long-term safety data. Regulators want years of evidence that implants stay safe and keep working.

forecasts.quote: Sample quote: we anticipate approval between 2029 and 2032.
Sample quote: most respondents expected approval in 2030 or 2031.

would_move_earlier.text: Sample. A fast-track designation from a major regulator.

would_move_later.text: Sample. A serious safety incident in an ongoing trial.

name: A non-invasive headset decodes text at typing speed

status_basis.text: Sample. Non-invasive decoding works for short, constrained phrases only.

summary.text: Sample. If you could type with thought without surgery, high-bandwidth interfaces would reach far more people.

success_criterion.text: Sample. 40 words per minute of free text with no implant, in a peer-reviewed study.

main_bottleneck.text: Sample. Signal quality through the skull.

forecasts.quote: Sample quote: non-invasive free-text decoding at typing speed looks achievable by 2028 to 2030.
Sample quote: the median answer for free-text decoding in everyday use, outside the lab, was 2042 to 2045.

basis.text: Sample. These two forecasts are about different things. The survey asked about decoding in everyday use outside the lab, a much harder target than our criterion of a peer-reviewed study, so we don't count it as disagreement.

would_move_earlier.text: Sample. A big jump in non-invasive signal quality, such as from new sensor types.

would_move_later.text: Sample. Results showing that decoding accuracy doesn't hold up outside the lab.

name: BCIs measurably help people keep economic agency

status_basis.text: Sample. No study has tried to measure this.

summary.text: Sample. The claim that BCIs could keep human labor valuable as AI improves. This is the step that would actually matter for the Intelligence Curse.

success_criterion.text: Sample. Not yet defined. The proposals we've found don't say what success would look like.

main_bottleneck.text: Sample. Unclear. It may not be technical at all.

would_move_earlier.text: Sample. A proposal that spells out how BCI users would stay competitive, and what to measure.

would_move_later.text: Sample. We haven't found anything specific yet.

name: A neuromorphic chip matches GPUs on energy per task

status_basis.text: Sample. Shown by more than one group on narrow benchmarks.
status_basis.quote: Sample quote: two independent groups reproduced the energy result on the same benchmark.

achieved_in_basis.text: Sample. First shown on a standard benchmark in 2024.
achieved_in_basis.quote: Sample quote: in 2024 the chip first matched GPU energy per inference on the benchmark.

summary.text: Sample. Brain-inspired hardware is already efficient on some tasks. Whether that helps alignment is a separate question.

success_criterion.text: Sample. Equal or lower energy per inference than a contemporary GPU on a standard benchmark.

main_bottleneck.text: Sample. Software and training tools, not the chips.

would_move_earlier.text: Sample. Already happened. Listed so the timeline shows what's done.

would_move_later.text: Sample. A failed replication on broader benchmarks.

name: Brain-like training shows a measurable alignment benefit

status_basis.text: Sample. The case is argued but not tested.
status_basis.quote: Sample quote: none of this has been tested empirically yet.

summary.text: Sample. The step where brain-inspired AI actually turns out easier to align than other AI, not just more efficient.

success_criterion.text: Sample. A brain-inspired system beats a matched conventional system on a standard alignment evaluation, replicated by an independent group.

main_bottleneck.text: Sample. Nobody agrees on which alignment evaluation would count.

basis.text: Sample. We start at 2035, later than the early-2030s forecast, because that forecast assumes an agreed alignment benchmark will exist and none does yet. No end date until there's a first result.

forecasts.quote: Sample quote: I'd expect a first clear result between 2030 and 2033.
Sample quote: the median answer was 2050 to 2060.

disagreement_note.text: Sample. One researcher expects first results in the early 2030s. The survey median is about twenty years later. Our range is a judgment call, so the badge stays up.

would_move_earlier.text: Sample. An agreed alignment benchmark that brain-inspired systems can be tested on.

would_move_later.text: Sample. Evidence that brain-like learning makes values harder to inspect, not easier.

artificial_minds_questions.text: Sample. If the system learns the way brains do, could it also have experiences that matter morally?
